sentiment.rationale: The document shows genuine operational momentum: revenue up 18%, core loss per share improved from ($1.13) to ($0.49), free cash flow usage improved from ($3.9B) to ($2.3B), and management describes a 'solid quarter' with 'recovery plan in full swing.' However, the forward outlook is mixed: the company reaffirmed its production rate plans but flagged a new, material risk from China tariffs affecting ~50 deliveries, and CFO Brian West declined to adjust the full-year free cash flow range pending more clarity. The positive operational trajectory is tempered by this new tariff uncertainty, resulting in a moderately positive score.

summary.revenue: $19.5 billion, up 18% from $16.6 billion in Q1 2024, 'primarily reflecting 130 commercial deliveries'
summary.eps: GAAP loss per share of ($0.16) and core (non-GAAP) loss per share of ($0.49), improved from ($0.56) and ($1.13) respectively in Q1 2024
summary.guidance: 737 production expected to reach 38 per month this year; 787 production expected to increase to 7 per month this year; 777X first delivery still anticipated in 2026; free cash flow full-year range not adjusted but CFO said 'we're not going to adjust that full year range right now'
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin 2.4% (vs -0.5% in Q1 2024); core operating margin 1.0% (vs -2.3% in Q1 2024); Commercial Airplanes operating margin (6.6)% (vs (24.6)%); Defense, Space & Security operating margin 2.5% (vs 2.2%); Global Services operating margin 18.6% (vs 18.2%)
key_risks: China tariffs: ~50 China deliveries at risk; customers in China have indicated they will not take delivery due to tariffs
Input tariffs: net annual impact of higher tariffs on input costs is 'less than $500 million annually'
Seat certification issues affecting some 787 deliveries expected to be a challenge for the balance of the year
SPS fire (Jenkintown fastener supplier) could create supply chain disruption
777X certification timeline still subject to FAA lead; first delivery in 2026
key_opportunities: F-47 win: selected by U.S. Air Force to design, build and deliver next-generation fighter aircraft
Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture for $10.55 billion expected to close by end of 2025, providing significant cash infusion
Strong demand environment: 'many customers who want near-term deliveries' and ability to redirect China-bound aircraft to other customers
Production rate increases planned for 737 (to 38/month, then to 42) and 787 (to 7/month, then higher)
Backlog grew to $545 billion, including over 5,600 commercial airplanes

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: CEO Kelly Ortberg stated 'our recovery plan is in full swing and showing signs that it's being effective' and 'I feel really good about our overall plan for the year, even though I expect the China situation will take away some of the headroom'
